title: The Liver
objective: After this level you can name the many jobs the liver does.
summary: The liver, the largest gland, meets absorbed nutrients first. It makes bile, stores glycogen and vitamins, clears wastes and old red blood cells, and can grow back after up to two-thirds is removed.

cards.headline: In Greek myth, an eagle ate Prometheus's liver. It kept growing back.
cards.body: That was Zeus's punishment: the liver regrew, so the torment never ended. Myth, of course. But real livers have a surprising talent for regrowing too. First, though: what does this organ actually do all day?

cards.headline: First stop after the gut
cards.body: Your liver is the largest gland in your body, about 1.2 to 1.6 kg in an adult. Remember Level 44? Blood from your intestines goes to the liver first, carrying the sugars and amino acids you just absorbed. The liver stores and processes those nutrients and sends them on to the rest of your body when they're needed. Every meal clears customs here.

items.label: Digestion
points: Makes bile, which helps digest fats
The gallbladder stores bile until you eat

items.label: Storage
points: Keeps glycogen, a store of energy

items.label: Clean-up
points: Breaks down old red blood cells
Removes wastes and harmful substances from the blood

mascot.line: Chef, pantry and cleaning crew in one organ. The liver does not do job descriptions.

cards.headline: The organ that grows back
cards.body: Surgeons can remove up to two-thirds of a healthy liver, and what's left grows back to about its original size, over weeks to months in people. The remaining liver cells divide and enlarge to rebuild it. It's Level 10's rule at work: new cells come only from existing cells. Prometheus had the right organ, just a faster schedule.

cards.headline: Liver: at work
learned: The largest gland, about 1.2 to 1.6 kg

questions.prompt: Which liver product helps your body digest fats?

options.label: Pepsin
options.rationale: Pepsin is a stomach enzyme for proteins.

options.label: Chyme
options.rationale: Chyme is the churned food leaving the stomach.

options.label: Saliva
options.rationale: Saliva comes from glands in the mouth.

questions.explanation: The liver makes bile, which helps digest fats; the gallbladder stores it between meals.

questions.prompt: Why does blood from the intestines pass through the liver before reaching the rest of the body?

options.label: So the liver can store and process the nutrients
So the liver can add stomach acid
options.rationale: The stomach makes its own acid.

options.label: So the liver can chew the food further
So the liver can make it into urine

questions.explanation: Absorbed nutrients reach the liver first, which stores, processes and sends them on when they're needed.

questions.prompt: Level 10's rule says new cells come only from existing cells. How does that show up when a liver regrows?

options.label: New liver cells arrive from the blood
options.rationale: They come from the liver itself.

options.label: Its remaining cells divide to rebuild it
It doesn't: livers can't regrow
options.rationale: A healthy liver can regrow after up to two-thirds is removed.

questions.explanation: After surgery, the remaining liver cells divide and enlarge until the liver is back to about its original size.
